text:
deploy-bot: INCIDENT P0 -> elevated error rate and timeouts on inference-router in us-west-2. auto-paging to @aisha (oncall). key signal: spike in 'agent_invoke' external calls and the JSON output serializer queue. ETA: under investigation.

Aisha (oncall): I'm seeing a big tail on token generation timeouts that correlate with requests that trigger external-action invocation (agenting). Latency and GPU stalls. Paging now.

Ben (eng-sre): Do we have a quick live mitigation? If we can limit or pause external action invocations and fallback to plain text responses that might drop load fast.

Carla (oncall-shift): Agree. We should avoid a full capacity scale right away. Options: throttle agent invocation rate globally, set per-account soft quotas, and disable machine-readable JSON outputs so the serializer doesn't do heavy post-processing.

Support-triage: CS report: 2 enterprise customers reporting timeouts for agent-driven flows (checkout assistants). They're blocked for 30+ minutes. Marta is preparing customer comms.

Marta (customer-success): I'm drafting a short note for impacted customers: "Temporary degradation for features that call external actions. We've applied mitigations and will follow up with timeline." Need confirm on scope so I can customize.

Aisha (oncall): Proposed immediate action plan (short window mitigation):
1) Apply global soft throttle for "agent invocation" requests to 0.5 rps default.
2) Apply targeted per-account lower qps for top consumers of agent features.
3) Disable the machine-readable JSON output mode for hosted routes (fallback to plain text).
4) Enable a text-only fallback route for clients that request structured responses.
5) Keep traffic routing and model variants untouched for now.

Ben (eng-sre): I'll execute step 1 and 3 now. Commands below — doing them from ops-jumpbox.

Ben (eng-sre): ```
# set global agent invocation rate
redwoodctl config set runtime.limits.agent_invocation_rps 0.5

# turn off machine-readable JSON generation for hosted routes
redwoodctl feature toggle --name=machine_readable_outputs --env=prod --off

# per-account example (apply to top noisy acct)
redwoodctl account update --id=acct-542 --agent-rps=0.2
```

Deploy-bot: Running change: redwoodctl config set runtime.limits.agent_invocation_rps 0.5 -> started.

Deploy-bot: Feature toggle request queued -> machine_readable_outputs OFF for prod. job_id=job-8721.

Aisha (oncall): I'm watching the dashboard. Looking at the "agent_invocation_latency" and "json-serializer-queue" metrics. Will call it if we see recovery.

Infra-bot: Alert: GPU utilization on the affected pool dropped 42% within 3 minutes; error-rate for agent-invoke down 58%. Presenting sample logs: 
```
[1829994384] ERROR servicer: agent-invoke timeout (5000ms) -> retry suppressed
[1829994390] WARN serializer: machine-json queue depth 120 -> now draining
```

Carla (oncall-shift): Seeing immediate improvement on tail latencies for non-agent routes. Agent-related throughput decreased as expected. Can we make the per-account limits more targeted so only noisy customers get reduced limits while preserving others?

Ben (eng-sre): Yes. I applied acct-542 and acct-781 limits. Will pre-authorize a small script to auto-apply top-10 noisy accounts if the metrics spike again. Script preview: 
```
# find top noisy accounts
redwoodctl metrics query --name=agent_invokes --group-by=account --top=10 --since=5m > noisy.txt
# apply 0.2 rps to each
cat noisy.txt | xargs -n1 -I{} redwoodctl account update --id={} --agent-rps=0.2
```

Marta (customer-success): Customer messages sent: enterprise-1 and enterprise-2. Response: both acknowledged and prefer a temporary mitigation over data loss. Will keep monitoring replies.

Support-triage: Creating INC ticket and noting mitigation steps in the summary. Ticket: INC-2027. Adding runbook link: https://go/runbooks/agent-overload.

Aisha (oncall): Monitoring window 30 minutes. If stable (errors < 5% baseline) we'll transition to observed-mode rate limits and re-enable machine_readable outputs in a phased canary after capacity checks. If not stable, escalate to infra scale-up and open a dedicated bridge.

Deploy-bot: job_id=job-8721 finished -> machine_readable_outputs toggled OFF across prod router; propagation 3 nodes pending.

Carla (oncall-shift): Metrics update at +10m: agent-invoke error-rate down 61%, avg p95 latency for non-agent clients within SLO. GPU queues less backpressure. Good sign.

Ben (eng-sre): Going to leave an automated watcher that will revert the account-level limits after 2 hours unless manually extended. Command applied.

Aisha (oncall): Handoff notes for night shift (carla):
- Monitor INC-2027 and charts (agent_invocation_latency, json-serializer-queue, gpu-backpressure).
- Keep per-account rate limiter script enabled but only run manually unless errors re-spike.
- If machine_readable_outputs toggled back on, do it via canary: toggle for 5% of routes then watch 15m.
- Customer comms owner: Marta; support thread pinned.

Carla (oncall-shift): Ack. I'll take the night handoff at 00:30 UTC. Will update INC-2027 every 30 minutes and notify if any regressions.

Marta (customer-success): Will follow up with customers in 1 hour with an update. Thanks team.

Deploy-bot: SUMMARY: mitigation applied -> global agent invocation soft throttle + per-account caps + machine_readable output mode turned off. Status: stabilizing. Reaction: :white_check_mark:

Aisha (oncall): Good job everyone. Keep ticket updated. If anything changes escalate to bridge.

Ben (eng-sre): Leaving monitoring hooks and alerts. Reverting plan if stable at +2h.

Carla (oncall-shift): Closing the slack coordination loop for now; will re-open if needed. :eyes:
